findings.reason: one sentence naming the existing persisted indexes, and why a live digest-keyed cache cannot be one of them, stops the system carrying a third representation of the same rows, which is the drift §3 and §4 exist to prevent.
findings.text: §3 places a new persisted index under the config-home cache without citing the two persisted plan-metadata stores the loader itself reads as fallback (state/<project>/index.json, state/<project>/projection.json)

findings.reason: the plan should name one row-application function the three call sites share; complexity spread across three wrappers over one operation is surface without depth, and a change to arrival accounting must otherwise be made in three implementations that can drift.
findings.text: §4 and §5 add applyIndexRowChanges and mergeDerived beside the first-paint assemble, three near-copies of map-row then key-by-arrivalKeyOf then hold-unknown-keys-as-arrivals then rebuild state.plans/attachment_relations/arrival

findings.reason: the adapter exists only because §8 forked the item shape; the plan should settle on one row shape, or state why the agent reader needs the wrapper, rather than add a thin translation layer with no depth.
findings.text: _indexed_item maps the index row's fields back into the discovery item shape serve._discover_plans_uncached already defines at serve.py:1782

findings.reason: the plan's §3/§4 design says the loader merges discovery's derived fields over the index's rows as one row set; leaving discovery building its own rows is what let the index and the served payload disagree on one document's created/edited stamps (the stat-vs-git drift the §3 review measured), and the plan should name metadata_index the row owner discovery extends rather than keep two builders in step by hand.
findings.text: the plan adds metadata_index._resource_row / _figure_row as a second per-document row builder beside the existing serve._discover_plans_uncached row builder (serve.py:1769-1858) and figures.figure_rows, all three calling resources.identify_resource + _plan_html.parse_meta + the stamp rule

findings.reason: two composers of the same derived payload over one index drift the same way the two row builders did; the plan should route the agent read through a shared composer, or say why the served payload cannot be built from the index too.
findings.text: §8 adds index_discovery as a second discovery-payload composer beside serve._discover_plans_uncached (serve.py:1745), both composing the project's own sprints/milestones/blockers/timeline for one project

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — docs/ui/state-loader.js spreads one row-application operation across assemble, mergeDerived and applyIndexRowChanges, so the arrival and state accounting has three copies.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan builds the per-document row set twice, in reckon/metadata_index.py and in serve._discover_plans_uncached (serve.py:1769), rather than naming the index as the row owner discovery extends.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds reckon/metadata_index.py, a persisted per-project metadata store, without citing the persisted plan metadata the codebase already keeps and the loader still falls back to (state/<project>/index.json, state/<project>/projection.json), so it never says why those cannot be extended.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — mcp_views._indexed_item re-shapes index rows back into the discovery item shape serve._discover_plans_uncached already builds, with no reason given why one shape cannot serve both readers.
